segments.start_exact:
Hard by a great forest dwelt a poor wood-cutter with his wife and his two
      children.
segments.end_exact: ‘But I feel very sorry for the poor children, all the same,’ said the man.
segments.summary: Starving woodcutter and wife debate abandoning children in forest; wife prevails and husband reluctantly consents.

gacd.goal: The wife wants to solve their starvation by getting rid of the children
gacd.action: She argues and pressures her husband to abandon the children in the forest
gacd.conflict: The husband resists, fearing for the children's lives

segments.reason: Opening scene unified by night/house; wife has goal, meets husband's resistance (conflict), and prevails (outcome), satisfying GACD.

segments.start_exact:
The two children had also not been able to sleep for hunger, and had heard
      what their stepmother had said
segments.end_exact:
throwing one of the white pebble-stones
      out of his pocket on the road.
segments.summary: Having overheard the plan, Hansel secretly gathers white pebbles at night and drops them along the path into the forest.

cohesion.place: The house and the path into the forest

gacd.goal: Hansel wants to save himself and Gretel from being lost
gacd.action: He collects pebbles and drops them to mark the trail while deceiving his parents
gacd.conflict: He must act secretly against the parents' plan and avoid detection

segments.reason: Continuous night-to-morning action with Hansel's countergoal against the parents' scheme; deception and secrecy provide conflict, satisfying GACD.

segments.start_exact: When they had reached the middle of the forest, the father said: ‘Now,
segments.end_exact:
we
      will come back and fetch you away.’
segments.summary: In the middle of the forest the parents build a fire and leave the children to rest while pretending to cut wood.
segments.reason: Brief transitional scene at a new place (middle of forest); mainly logistical setup without on-stage conflict, so narrative_scene.

segments.start_exact:
Hansel and Gretel sat by the fire, and when noon came, each ate a little
      piece of bread
segments.end_exact:
for it had cut him to
      the heart to leave them behind alone.
segments.summary: The children wait, sleep, then use the moonlit pebbles to find their way home, arriving at their father's house.

cohesion.time: From noon through the night to daybreak

gacd.action: They wait for the moon and follow the pebble trail through the forest
gacd.conflict: Darkness, being lost, Gretel's fear of not finding the way

segments.reason: Goal of getting home, action of following pebbles, conflict of darkness/being lost, and successful return; a completed dramatic scene.

segments.start_exact: Not long afterwards, there was once more great dearth throughout the land,
segments.end_exact:
they lay
      down beneath a tree and fell asleep.
segments.summary: New famine; parents again abandon children. Hansel drops bread crumbs but birds eat them, leaving the children lost in the deep forest.

cohesion.time: The second abandonment, over several days
cohesion.place: The house and deeper into the forest

gacd.goal: Hansel again tries to secure a way home
gacd.action: Locked in, he crumbles bread on the path instead of pebbles
gacd.conflict: The door is locked and birds eat the crumbs

segments.reason: Second abandonment sequence unified by the crumb plan; Hansel's goal meets obstacles (locked door, birds) ending in disaster (lost), satisfying GACD.

segments.start_exact: It was now three mornings since they had left their father’s house.
segments.end_exact:
lay down in them, and thought they were in
      heaven.
segments.summary: Lost and starving, the children follow a bird to a gingerbread house, eat from it, and are taken in by a seemingly kind old woman.

cohesion.place: Deep forest and the witch's candy house

segments.reason: Discovery of the house and reception is largely descriptive/transitional with the interior verses; no sustained on-stage conflict/outcome, so narrative_scene.

segments.start_exact:
The old woman had only pretended to be so kind; she was in reality a
      wicked witch
segments.summary: The witch imprisons Hansel to fatten and eat him and enslaves Gretel; Hansel fools her with a bone, but she resolves to kill him anyway.

gacd.goal: The witch wants to fatten and eat Hansel
gacd.action: She imprisons him, checks his finger daily, and forces Gretel to serve
gacd.conflict: Hansel deceives her with a bone so she cannot tell he stays thin

segments.reason: Captivity scene with witch's goal, action, and conflict via Hansel's trickery; interim outcome (she decides to kill him regardless), a dramatic scene.

segments.start_exact: Early in the morning, Gretel had to go out and hang up the cauldron with
segments.end_exact: that we may get out of the witch’s forest.’
segments.summary: Gretel tricks the witch into the oven and burns her, frees Hansel, and they take the witch's treasure to leave.

gacd.goal: Gretel wants to escape and save Hansel
gacd.action: She tricks the witch into the oven and bolts the door, then frees Hansel
gacd.conflict: The witch intends to bake Gretel; a deadly struggle of wits

segments.reason: Climactic scene: Gretel's goal, deceptive action, lethal conflict with the witch, and successful escape with treasure; clear GACD.

whosoever catches it, may make himself a big fur

segments.summary: The children reach a water they can't cross, a duck ferries them over, and they return home to their father with riches; the wife is dead.

cohesion.place: The great water and the father's house

gacd.goal: Return home safely with the treasure
gacd.action: They enlist a duck to ferry them across the water and journey home
gacd.conflict: An impassable stretch of water blocks their way

segments.reason: Final journey with an obstacle (water) overcome by the duck, leading to a happy homecoming; goal/action/conflict/outcome present, ending the tale.
